notes: stdout carries only the result document; diagnostics and errors go to stderr.
Every JSON document has a "schema" field. New fields may appear without a version change; a breaking change bumps the version.
Enums are open: handle values you don't know.
Money is in integer micros of USD (1 USD = 1,000,000 micros), with a "currency" field.
Unknown values are null, with a *_unavailable_reason field, never 0.
vitko never prompts. Missing input is a usage error (exit code 2).

commands.summary: Estimate what your GitHub Actions usage would cost on Vitko Runners.
commands.description:
Reads GitHub's usage report and prices the Linux x64 minutes at the Vitko list price, next to what GitHub charged. It runs on your machine: the report is never uploaded.
Get the report from GitHub: Settings > Billing and licensing > Usage > Get usage report (the summarized report is enough). Or pass --from-github to fetch it with the GitHub CLI (needs an organization owner or billing manager).
Each month gets its own free minutes. The result is an upper bound, because GitHub rounds each job up to whole minutes and Vitko bills per second.

args.name: file
args.summary: GitHub usage report: the CSV, or the JSON from the billing usage API. Several files are fine.

flags.name: from-github
flags.summary: Fetch the usage of this GitHub organization with the GitHub CLI (gh) instead of reading files.

flags.name: month
flags.summary: With --from-github: the month(s) to fetch. Default: last month.

flags.name: by-repo
flags.summary: Also list Linux x64 minutes per repository.

flags.name: per-second-factor
flags.summary: Illustrative ratio of per-second time to GitHub's rounded minutes, in (0, 1]. 1 is the upper bound.

commands.description: The public list price, how time is billed, the free minutes and the dated GitHub price it is compared with.

commands.summary: Switch a repository's GitHub Actions jobs to Vitko runners.
commands.description:
Changes `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` to `vitko-ubuntu-24.04` in .github/workflows. Only that value changes; comments and formatting stay as they are. Jobs it can't change safely (expressions and matrices, other operating systems, self-hosted runners, runner groups, custom labels, workflows from other repositories) are listed with the reason, and left alone.
Running it again changes nothing. --dry-run shows the diff without writing. --check exits with code 10 if anything would change. --pr makes the change on a fresh copy of the default branch and opens a pull request with your own git and GitHub CLI (gh) sign-in; your working copy isn't touched.

args.name: path
args.summary: Repository directory, or one workflow file. Default: the current directory.

flags.name: workflow
flags.summary: Only these workflow files (name or path).

flags.name: label
flags.summary: The runs-on label to switch to.

flags.name: dry-run
flags.summary: Show the diff without writing anything.

flags.name: check
flags.summary: Write nothing; exit with code 10 if anything would change.

flags.name: pr
flags.summary: Open a pull request instead of editing the working copy.

flags.name: base
flags.summary: With --pr: the branch to change and target. Default: the repository's default branch.

flags.name: branch
flags.summary: With --pr: the name of the new branch.

examples: vitko runners repos switch path/to/repo --workflow ci.yml --job test
